scope.notCovered: This record does not certify all230 catalog entries, absent 3D/fog entity systems or unspecified infinite combinations.

catalogClauses.descriptionEn: Lifestealer's attacks deal damage and provide heal for a percentage of his target's max health.
catalogClauses.superEn: Super: Grants Open Wounds: rends an enemy unit, granting 50% lifesteal to units attacking that target, and dealing 2% of the target's max health per attack from real heroes. After the target receives 500 damage, Open Wounds festers and spreads a random enemy in a 700 radius.

sources.observation: The pinned shipped ability KV supplies native cast points, ranges, attack reduction, tick intervals, upgrade prototypes and the one-level Open Wounds native definition. It does not provide executable AA custom Lua.

sources.observation: The 6.84 change makes Feast ordinary attack bonus damage eligible for critical strike and cleave.
sources.versionContext: Dated 2015 pre-2023 attack-composition change. AA equal damage/heal percentages remain authoritative.

sources.observation: The old Feast description separates max-health restoration from actual damage and puts its bonus into the attack so ordinary lifesteal, critical strike and cleave can use it. It excludes allied, ward and building targets.
sources.versionContext: The page explicitly bounds this old ability to versions 6.49 through 7.22h. It supports an older mechanism prototype, not blanket certification of all 2023 branches. Its wording on percentage damage amplification conflicts with the current conditional-bonus page and is retained as an open version question.

sources.observation: The current conditional attack bonus participates in critical strike, cleave, physical block and ordinary attack lifesteal. Its own max-health restoration occurs before the attack independently of target damage or barriers. Percentage amplification of main damage excludes the conditional bonus.
sources.versionContext: Current indexed primary Wiki. Critical/cleave composition has explicit pre-2023 support; the percentage-amplification branch is still pending because the old version-bounded page differs. Modern innate kill-health behavior is excluded.

sources.observation: The dated 2019-12-09 change fixes Feast lifesteal amplification. June 2022 Open Wounds fixes identify special health-removal and return-damage interactions.
sources.versionContext: Pre-2023 dated primary changelog. The individual exceptional damage sources still require separate result qualification; it is not proof that every reflected/health-removal packet has one shared policy.

sources.observation: The current attack-modifier list excludes intrinsic Feast from illusion copying.
sources.versionContext: Current primary indexed page; the exact historical list and AA custom global-aura illusion eligibility are not certified from this modern list.

sources.observation: Original player inputs and battle seed reconstruct the same deterministic simulation and effective statistical ledger. This is a project serialization contract, not native Dota evidence.
sources.versionContext: C4 baseline serialization interface; these tests exercise the registered C6 programs and their current source-owned statuses using original inputs rather than injecting saved runtime ledgers.

sources.observation: The 2014-11-19 change defers both damage and healing resolution until invulnerability ends. The 2014-11-20 fix stops ongoing invisibility and doubled healing during that wait. The 2015-12-16 change removes continuous dispelling after the initial cast. Talents in 7.29 and 7.26c supply armor and extra-duration prototypes.
sources.versionContext: Explicit pre-2023 dated rules. AA uses +15 armor, +1.5 seconds and -30 seconds cooldown, even where native talents or base duration differ.

sources.observation: The earlier directly read historical Oracle capture distinguishes False Promise damage prevention, its special Borrowed Time interaction, ordinary barriers and later health-removal settlement. Existing finite settlement tests are background evidence, not a substitute for this group clause review.
sources.versionContext: HTTP200 historical 2023-02-15 capture metadata reused from settlement-engine.json. No new Wayback request was issued while the service returned 429. Later barrier reorder and modern Scepter redesign are excluded.
